proofs.proof_tex:
Selected-table positivity gives \(r_e>0\), \(T_e(w,z)>0\), and
\[
v_e(z)=\sum_wT_e(w,z)>0                                      \tag{1}
\]
for every \(e\) and \(z\).  Fix a cell with \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\).  By the definition of \(\mathcal C_A(T)\), every legal point satisfies
\[
T_e=b_i a_{ei}^{\top}+b_j a_{ej}^{\top},
\qquad
a_{ei}+a_{ej}=v_e.                                           \tag{2}
\]
The right side of the first equality is a sum of two rank-one matrices, so \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)\leq2\).  Positivity in (1) rules out rank zero.  Thus an observed rank exceeding two makes both cycle fibers empty.

Suppose first that \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)=2\), and define the normalized observed columns
\[
c_{ez}=\frac{T_e(\cdot,z)}{v_e(z)}.
\]
Division is legal by (1).  Equation (2) gives
\[
c_{ez}=\lambda_{ez}b_i+(1-\lambda_{ez})b_j,
\qquad
\lambda_{ez}=\frac{a_{ei}(z)}{v_e(z)}\in[0,1].               \tag{3}
\]
Rank two forces \(b_i\neq b_j\).  Conversely, let two endpoints on the observed affine line contain every \(c_{ez}\) in their closed segment.  Choose a coordinate \(h_e\) for which \(b_i(h_e)\neq b_j(h_e)\).  The unique coefficients are
\[
a_{ei}(z)=v_e(z)
 \frac{c_{ez}(h_e)-b_j(h_e)}{b_i(h_e)-b_j(h_e)},
\qquad
a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)-a_{ei}(z).                                  \tag{4}
\]
The pivot denominator is nonzero by its choice, and the segment inequalities make both terms nonnegative.  Reversing the endpoints gives exactly the second orientation.  For each \(z\), the positive sum in (2) has precisely the three support alternatives \(a_{ei}(z)=0\), \(a_{ej}(z)=0\), or both coefficients positive.  Hence the two orientations and their coordinatewise support refinements exhaust the rank-two cell.

If \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)=1\), the established rank-one normal-form lemma supplies the unique positive column point \(c_e\) and proves that the modes \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) are disjoint and exhaustive.  Its coordinatewise refinement of \(\mathrm E\) retains the alternatives \(s_e(z)=0\), \(0<s_e(z)<v_e(z)\), and \(s_e(z)=v_e(z)\).  Thus inactive rows, equal endpoints, and every forced-zero boundary face are retained without division.

Take the product of the four local lists and identify the two occurrences of each response endpoint \(b_i\).  Endpoint simplex and support conditions, equality or inequality of endpoints, incidence with an observed affine line, segment order, and the equations in (2) and (4) are polynomial sign conditions after a denominator is cleared only on the chart recording its nonzero sign.  The preceding exhaustive alternatives show that every point of \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) belongs to at least one resulting chart.  Conversely, substituting a chart point in (2), together with its simplex and support conditions, proves membership in \(\mathcal C_A(T)\).  Therefore
\[
\bigcup_\chi X^A_\chi=\mathcal C_A(T).                      \tag{5}
\]

For design B, fix a design-A cycle point and a positive projective coordinate \(\rho\).  The established residual-forest theorem proves, at every response type, the exhaustive alternatives that both incident residuals vanish or that they are nonzero and negatively proportional; the case in which exactly one residual vanishes is infeasible.  In an active state the first nonzero residual coordinate is a lexicographic pivot, and its sign yields a finite refinement.  The induced positive margin ratios propagate from one positive scale on every forest component, and an active cycle is consistent exactly when its ratio product is one.  Normalization fixes the remaining common scale.  Finally, instrument relevance is the finite disjunction
\[
q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z)>0
\quad\hbox{or}\quad
q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z)<0                                  \tag{6}
\]
over unordered distinct pairs \(\{z,z'\}\).  The residual-forest theorem says that these conditions are necessary and sufficient for the positive margins, the response-level shared-\(Z\) equations, and relevance.  Consequently
\[
\bigcup_\chi X^B_\chi=\mathcal C_B(T).                      \tag{7}
\]

It remains to prove the claimed finite counts.  Each proxy endpoint has a nonempty support, so the four shared endpoints have at most
\[
(2^{\ell}-1)^4                                               \tag{8}
\]
labeled support patterns.  A rank-two local library has \(2\cdot3^k\) oriented support modes.  The rank-one library has \(3^k\) refined \(\mathrm E\) modes and the three additional modes \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm D\).  Listing both possible positive ranks before the observed rank is consulted therefore uses at most
\[
2\cdot3^k+3^k+3=3^{k+1}+3                                  \tag{9}
\]
local templates.  Multiplying (8) by the fourth power of (9) gives \(M_A\).  In design B, each of the four response links has one zero-residual state or \(2(k-1)\) active pivot-and-sign states, for \((2k-1)^4\) joint labels.  The unordered relevance pair and the sign in (6) have \(2\binom{k}{2}=k(k-1)\) labels.  Multiplication gives \(M_B\).

Every coefficient in these polynomial conditions is obtained from \(T\) and \(v\).  Since \(T_e=p_e/r_e\), the nonzero normalizers \(r_e\) and all chart coefficients belong to \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  The list is finite, includes every support face by (3)--(7), and can therefore be sampled or labeled over that field, with real-univariate and Thom data when a diagnostic sample is algebraic.  Equations (5) and (7) prove exact structural exhaustiveness.  None of these enumerations is used in the raw-fiber decision proved below, so the atlas is an optional diagnostic as claimed.

The supplied design-A margin must be validated before the normalized cycle fiber is used.  The established design-A nonemptiness criterion gives the equivalence
\[
\mathcal F_A(p,m)\neq\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}
\ \hbox{and}\ 
\mathcal C_A(T)\neq\varnothing.                             \tag{10}
\]
For design B, surjectivity in the cycle-to-SCM lift gives
\[
\mathcal F_B(p)\neq\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal C_B(T)\neq\varnothing.                             \tag{11}
\]
Thus failure of the margin test in design A, or emptiness of the applicable raw cycle fiber, is exactly incompatibility.  Its target image has cardinality zero, so it is not rigid under the cardinality-one definition.

Assume now that the applicable raw fiber is nonempty, and denote it by \(X\).  The defining simplex conditions, nonnegativity or strict positivity conditions, factorization equations, and, in design B, shared-\(Z\) equations and the finite relevance disjunction make \(X\) a bounded semialgebraic set over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  The target map
\[
f(x)=\tau_C(x)=
\left(\sum_z a_{11,2}(z),\sum_z a_{00,2}(z)\right)           \tag{12}
\]
is polynomial.  Apply the established one-sample/all-chart rigidity lemma to the one-element family \(X_1=X\).  Its initial bounded-algebraic-sampling call returns \(x_0\in X\) and fixes \(t_0=f(x_0)\).  Its only existential refinement is
\[
R(x_0)=X\cap\{x:\|f(x)-t_0\|_2^2>0\}.                     \tag{13}
\]
We also verify the equivalence directly.  If \(R(x_0)=\varnothing\), every \(x\in X\) has \(\|f(x)-t_0\|_2^2=0\), hence \(f(x)=t_0\) and \(f(X)=\{t_0\}\).  Conversely, if \(f(X)=\{t_0\}\), no point can satisfy the strict inequality in (13), so \(R(x_0)=\varnothing\).  If (13) is nonempty, its sampled point \(x_1\) satisfies \(f(x_1)\neq f(x_0)\).  This proves the necessary-and-sufficient test with exactly one raw-fiber sampling call and one raw-fiber existential call.

The cycle-to-SCM lift is onto and target preserving.  Combining it with (10)--(12) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal T_A(p,m)
 &=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\},\\
\mathcal T_B(p)
 &=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a,m,g,\pi)\in\mathcal C_B(T)\}.
\end{aligned}                                                \tag{14}
\]
Consequently (13) is empty exactly when the appropriate causal target set in (14) is a singleton.  If it is nonempty, lift \(x_0\) and \(x_1\) separately.  The resulting parameters lie in the same full fiber, so they have identical selected observables and, in design A, the identical supplied margin \(m\); target preservation and (13) give different values of \(\tau\).  These are the required legal full-SCM twins.  If both cycle points belong to interior support charts, the established positive-lift lemma makes every response mass, proxy and instrument kernel, treatment probability, and selection probability strictly interior.  That lemma gives no such conclusion on a boundary face, which proves exactly the stated qualification.

The effective semialgebraic sampling lemma returns \(x_0\) as a real-univariate representation with Thom signs over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  Since (12) consists of linear coordinate sums, \(t_0\) lies in the same finite real algebraic field.  The second call is made over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)\) and returns the same type of representation for \(x_1\), if it exists.  A rational expression over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) is used only when field arithmetic actually constructs one; otherwise square-free univariate and Thom data select the unique ordered real value.  For rational input, the cited square-free-factorization and root-isolation procedures give an integer polynomial and rational isolating data.  This establishes every exact-output clause.  Structural labels may be attached afterward using the exhaustive atlas, but the proof of (13) and the mandatory computation never enumerate a chart or a connected component.

Let \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\).  We first count a direct polynomial presentation of each raw fiber.  In design A, the four endpoint vectors \(b_i\) contribute \(4\ell\) variables, and the two incident coefficient vectors in each of four cells contribute \(8k\), giving
\[
N_A=4\ell+8k.                                                \tag{15}
\]
The endpoint nonnegativity and four normalizations use \(4\ell+4\) sign atoms.  Coefficient nonnegativity uses \(8k\), the four equations \(a_{ei}+a_{ej}=v_e\) use \(4k\), and the factorization equations use \(4k\ell\).  Therefore
\[
S_A=4k\ell+4\ell+12k+4.                                    \tag{16}
\]
Every factorization equation is bilinear in \((b,a)\), and all other design-A atoms are linear, so \(D_A=2\).

The raw design-B presentation adds the four margin coordinates, the \(k\) common-instrument coordinates, and the four response masses.  Hence
\[
N_B=N_A+4+k+4=4\ell+9k+8.                                  \tag{17}
\]
Margin positivity and normalization add five atoms, common-instrument positivity and normalization add \(k+1\), response-mass nonnegativity and normalization add five, and the response-level shared-\(Z\) equations add \(4k\).  Relevance can be written as the disjunction, over unordered pairs \(\{z,z'\}\), of the two strict signs of
\[
q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z).                                    \tag{18}
\]
Allowing two sign atoms even for both orders gives the conservative addition \(2k(k-1)\).  Adding these quantities to (16) proves
\[
S_B\leq4k\ell+2k^2+4\ell+15k+15.                           \tag{19}
\]
The shared-\(Z\) equations are quadratic because they contain \(m_ea_{ei}(z)\) and \(\pi_i g(z)\).  By the definition of \(q^X\), expression (18) is cubic after substitution, and no raw atom has larger degree.  Thus \(D_B=3\).  The target in (12) is linear, so its squared-distance inequality has degree two and does not enlarge either degree bound.

The effective semialgebraic sampling lemma, applied once to the raw design-\(d\) fiber over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), generates at most \(A_{S,d}\) records.  When the fiber is nonempty, let \(\xi\) be a primitive element for the sampled point \(x_0\).  The same lemma gives
\[
[\mathbb K_{\zeta}(\xi):\mathbb K_{\zeta}]
\leq D_{S,d}.                                                \tag{20}
\]
The two coordinates of \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\) are linear sums of coordinates of \(x_0\), whence
\[
\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)\subseteq\mathbb K_{\zeta}(\xi),
\qquad
[\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0):\mathbb K_{\zeta}]
\leq D_{S,d}.                                                \tag{21}
\]
There is then one existential-realizability call, over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)\), on the raw fiber plus its one squared-distance atom.  It generates at most \(A_{E,d}\) records.  If it returns a witness with primitive element \(\upsilon\), then
\[
[\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0,\upsilon):
  \mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)]\leq D_{E,d}.                      \tag{22}
\]
Choose a spanning set of at most \(D_{S,d}\) elements for \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)\) over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), and a spanning set of at most \(D_{E,d}\) elements for \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0,\upsilon)\) over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)\).  Their pairwise products span the larger field over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), so (21)--(22) give
\[
[\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0,\upsilon):\mathbb K_{\zeta}]
\leq D_{S,d}D_{E,d}=\mathcal D_d.                           \tag{23}
\]
Every returned coordinate \(u\) lies in this field.  In a vector space of dimension at most \(\mathcal D_d\), the \(\mathcal D_d+1\) elements \(1,u,\ldots,u^{\mathcal D_d}\) are linearly dependent over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  Hence a nonzero polynomial of degree at most \(\mathcal D_d\) annihilates \(u\), and its minimal polynomial has no larger degree.  The cited tower-flattening, square-free-factorization, Thom-sign, and isolation procedures do not increase the field degree.  This proves the algebraic-degree bound by explicit multiplication of the two sequential relative degrees.  The two fixed status/output records together with the two algorithmic bounds give
\[
R_d=2+A_{S,d}+A_{E,d}.                                      \tag{24}
\]
There is no multiplication by a chart count because both calls use the single raw fiber.

For completeness, the diagnostic template count follows from the mixed-support structural theorem:
\[
M_A=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4,
\qquad
M_B=M_Ak(k-1)(2k-1)^4.                                     \tag{25}
\]
This finite list terminates if requested, but (25) does not occur in (23) or (24), and none of its residual, pivot, forest, or support variables occurs in (15) or (17).

Put \(Q=k\ell+k^2+\ell+1\).  Equations (15)--(19) imply, after increasing a universal constant \(C\),
\[
N_d\leq CQ,
\qquad S_d\leq CQ,
\qquad D_d\leq3.                                           \tag{26}
\]
The published coordinatewise nondecreasing sampling and existential bounds in the effective semialgebraic lemma therefore give
\[
A_{S,d},D_{S,d},A_{E,d},D_{E,d}
\leq2^{CQ^C}.                                                \tag{27}
\]
Substitution into (23)--(24), followed by another enlargement of \(C\), proves
\[
R_{k,\ell}\leq2^{CQ^C},
\qquad
\mathcal D_{k,\ell}\leq2^{CQ^C}.                           \tag{28}
\]
For arbitrary real input, the only observable normalizations are divisions by \(r_e>0\), guaranteed by selected-table positivity.  Hence the raw coefficients lie in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  The cited arithmetic, order, sign-determination, sampling, and real-root procedures terminate over the assumed effective oracle field.  Since there are only the two calls above, relative termination follows.

Suppose next that every rational input numerator and denominator has binary length at most \(L\).  Reconstructing the deleted simplex coordinates, forming each positive \(r_e\), dividing to obtain \(T_e\) and \(v_e\), and clearing those nonzero observable denominators in polynomials of degree at most three uses at most a quadratic number of elementary rational sums and products in \(Q\).  The conservative bound
\[
h_0=64Q^2(L+1)                                               \tag{29}
\]
therefore dominates the binary length of every cleared integer coefficient.  No latent pivot denominator is introduced by the raw presentation.

The integer-height part of the cited sampling result gives
\[
h_{S,d}=\mathsf{Samp}_h(N_d,S_d,D_d,h_0).                    \tag{30}
\]
The second formula contains \(t_0\), represented in an extension of degree at most \(D_{S,d}\) and height at most \(h_{S,d}\).  Applying the relative existential height bound gives
\[
h_{E,d}=\mathsf{Exist}_h
(N_d,S_d+1,D_d;h_0,h_{S,d},D_{S,d}).                         \tag{31}
\]
Finally, multiplication matrices in dimension at most \(\mathcal D_d\), followed by square-free factorization and isolation, give
\[
h_{F,d}=\mathsf{Flat}_h
(\mathcal D_d,h_{S,d}+h_{E,d}+1).                            \tag{32}
\]
Equations (30)--(32) are sequential: the second-stage bound includes the first extension, and the flattening bound includes both heights and the product degree.  The height envelopes in the cited lemma, (26), and (27) imply, after one final enlargement of \(C\),
\[
H_{k,\ell}(L)
\leq\bigl[64Q^2(L+2)\bigr]^{2^{CQ^C}}.                     \tag{33}
\]
This is a separate rational-height guarantee; it is not identified with the singly exponential record and degree bounds in (28).  Square-free normalization and rational isolation give the stated exact representations.  All rational subroutines are finite, so the rational-input Turing implementation terminates.  The full-rigidity theorem proves that these two raw-fiber calls decide the causal target, while (25) remains solely an optional structural diagnostic.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every fixed finite \((\mathcal W,\mathcal Z)\), the following finite structural atlas is exhaustive.  It rejects a cell whose observed matrix has rank exceeding two.  A rank-two cell is represented by its two oriented segment modes, refined by all coefficient-support faces.  A rank-one cell is represented by the disjoint \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes of the rank-one normal-form lemma, with the \(\mathrm E\) mode split coordinatewise.  Products of the four local modes use one shared variable \(b_i\) at each response vertex, fix proxy supports, and retain endpoint equalities and inequalities, observed-line incidences, and guarded nonzero pivots as polynomial sign atoms.  If \(X^A_\chi\) denotes the resulting design-A charts, then
\[
\bigcup_\chi X^A_\chi=\mathcal C_A(T).
\]
In design B, adjoining \(\rho\), the zero-residual or active negatively proportional state at each response type, lexicographic nonzero pivots, forest propagation, active-cycle product-one constraints, positive component scales, normalization, and a signed relevance witness gives charts satisfying
\[
\bigcup_\chi X^B_\chi=\mathcal C_B(T).
\]
Writing \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), the numbers of labeled templates are at most
\[
M_A=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4,
\qquad
M_B=M_A\,k(k-1)(2k-1)^4.
\]
Every chart has a finite Boolean semialgebraic description over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), including every zero-support and coincident-endpoint face.  Thus the atlas is an exact field-tier structural classification and may be used to label or diagnose a raw-fiber output.  It is not a computational prerequisite for the direct raw-fiber rigidity decision made by \(\mathscr A\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current statement makes the exhaustive structural atlas carry the rigidity decision.  The directed repair narrows that theorem to the exact mixed-support structural classification and its finite diagnostic template bound, leaving the logically independent raw-fiber decision to the rigidity theorem.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For design A, \(\mathscr A\) first tests \(m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\).  If this test fails, or if the single bounded-algebraic-sampling call on the raw legal fiber \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) reports emptiness, then \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)=\varnothing\); the input is reported as incompatible and is not rigid under \(|\mathcal T_A(p,m)|=1\).  Otherwise let \(x_0\in\mathcal C_A(T)\) be the returned sample and set \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\).  Then \(|\mathcal T_A(p,m)|=1\) if and only if the single raw-fiber refinement
\[
\mathcal C_A(T)\cap\left\{x:
(\tau_{C,1}(x)-t_{0,1})^2+(\tau_{C,2}(x)-t_{0,2})^2>0
\right\}
\]
is empty.  For design B, emptiness of the single sampling call on \(\mathcal C_B(T)\) is equivalent to \(\mathcal F_B(p)=\varnothing\), and, on a nonempty fiber, the analogous single refinement is empty if and only if \(|\mathcal T_B(p)|=1\).

For an arbitrary real input \(\zeta\), a rigid value is returned as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only when the compiler constructs such an expression; every other value is returned as a uniquely ordered real element of a finite algebraic extension, encoded by a square-free real-univariate polynomial over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), rational coordinate functions, and Thom sign data.  For rational \(\zeta\), the encoding may be normalized to a square-free integer polynomial and rational isolating data.  Every nonrigid output contains two legal full SCMs with identical observables and identical supplied margins when margins are supplied, but different \(\tau\).  If both raw-fiber witnesses lie in interior support charts, their full-SCM lifts can be chosen strictly positive; no strict-positivity claim is made for a witness on a boundary face.  The exhaustive structural atlas may label the output diagnostically, but neither its enumeration nor a connected-component description is used in the rigidity decision.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current statement unnecessarily requires an emptiness and unequal-target test on every structural chart.  Since the already-defined raw legal fiber is one bounded semialgebraic set, the same target claim follows from one sampling call and one one-copy unequal-target call on that fiber, with the existing compatibility and lift guarantees unchanged.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Put \(k=|\mathcal Z|\), \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), and
\[
\begin{array}{lll}
N_A=4\ell+8k,&
S_A=4k\ell+4\ell+12k+4,&
D_A=2,\\
N_B=4\ell+9k+8,&
S_B=4k\ell+2k^2+4\ell+15k+15,&
D_B=3.
\end{array}
\]
The raw design-A fiber has a Boolean semialgebraic description with at most \((N_A,S_A,D_A)\) variables, polynomial sign atoms, and polynomial degree, and the raw design-B fiber has one with at most \((N_B,S_B,D_B)\).  The single squared unequal-target atom does not increase either degree bound.  For \(d\in\{A,B\}\), let
\[
(A_{S,d},D_{S,d})=\mathsf{Samp}(N_d,S_d,D_d),
\qquad
(A_{E,d},D_{E,d})=\mathsf{Exist}(N_d,S_d+1,D_d),
\]
where these are coordinatewise nondecreasing published record-count and relative algebraic-degree bounds for bounded algebraic sampling and existential realizability over the current coefficient field.  Define
\[
R_d=2+A_{S,d}+A_{E,d},
\qquad
\mathcal D_d=D_{S,d}D_{E,d},
\qquad
R_{k,\ell}=\max_{d\in\{A,B\}}R_d,
\qquad
\mathcal D_{k,\ell}=\max_{d\in\{A,B\}}\mathcal D_d.
\]
Then \(R_d\) bounds all algebraic sample and decision records generated by the mandatory design-\(d\) raw-fiber path, and \(\mathcal D_d\) bounds the degree over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) of every final real-univariate target or witness coordinate after tower normalization.  These bounds contain no structural-template multiplier and no chart auxiliary variables.  The optional diagnostic atlas nevertheless terminates and has at most
\[
M_A=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4,
\qquad
M_B=M_A\,k(k-1)(2k-1)^4
\]
labeled templates.

If \(Q=k\ell+k^2+\ell+1\), there is a universal constant \(C\geq1\), independent of \(k\), \(\ell\), and the input, such that
\[
R_{k,\ell}\leq2^{CQ^C},
\qquad
\mathcal D_{k,\ell}\leq2^{CQ^C}.
\]
Over an arbitrary real input field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), the computation terminates relative to effective field arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles.

For rational input coordinates whose numerators and denominators have binary length at most \(L\), set
\[
h_0=64Q^2(L+1),
\qquad
h_{S,d}=\mathsf{Samp}_h(N_d,S_d,D_d,h_0),
\]
\[
h_{E,d}=\mathsf{Exist}_h(N_d,S_d+1,D_d;h_0,h_{S,d},D_{S,d}),
\qquad
h_{F,d}=\mathsf{Flat}_h(\mathcal D_d,h_{S,d}+h_{E,d}+1),
\]
and
\[
H_{k,\ell}(L)=
\max_{d\in\{A,B\}}\max\{h_{S,d},h_{E,d},h_{F,d}\}.
\]
After flattening the extension tower and clearing only nonzero observable normalizing denominators, every algebraic target or witness coordinate has a square-free integer polynomial of degree at most \(\mathcal D_{k,\ell}\) and rational isolating data of binary length at most \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\).  After enlarging the same universal constant if necessary,
\[
H_{k,\ell}(L)
\leq
\bigl[64Q^2(L+2)\bigr]^{2^{CQ^C}}.
\]
Thus the mandatory decision consists of one raw-fiber sampling call followed, when nonempty, by one raw-fiber unequal-target existential call.  It does not enumerate charts, describe connected components, project a target image, or use a generic two-copy classifier.  A rational-input Turing implementation terminates.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current complexity statement charges the mandatory decision for every optional structural template and includes chart auxiliaries.  The repaired claim counts the two raw-fiber calls, proves raw degrees two and three in the two designs, multiplies the two sequential extension degrees, and retains the template count only as a diagnostic bound.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Define the mandatory decision path of \(\mathscr A\) directly on the raw legal cycle fiber.  In design A, first test \(m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\); failure is reported as incompatibility.  Otherwise put \(X=\mathcal C_A(T)\).  In design B put \(X=\mathcal C_B(T)\).  Make one bounded-algebraic-sampling call on \(X\).  If \(X\) is empty, report incompatibility.  Otherwise take the returned point \(x_0\), put \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\), and make one existential-realizability call on
\[
X\cap\left\{x:
(\tau_{C,1}(x)-t_{0,1})^2+(\tau_{C,2}(x)-t_{0,2})^2>0
\right\}.
\]
If this refinement is empty, return \(t_0\); otherwise return its sampled point together with \(x_0\) and lift them to legal target-changing full SCMs.  Separately, \(\mathscr A\) may enumerate labeled candidate charts formed from the oriented rank-two, \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) rank-one, support-face, shared-endpoint, and design-B residual-forest modes as structural diagnostics; that enumeration is not consulted by the mandatory rigidity decision.  All symbolic arithmetic is over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), or over the finite real algebraic extension generated by \(t_0\) during the single refinement test.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The mandatory exact decision can operate directly on the already-defined raw legal fiber.  The corrected construction separates this two-call engine from the exhaustive structural atlas, which remains available for labels and diagnostics.

proposed.name: Raw-fiber rigidity compiler and diagnostic mixed-support atlas
proposed.construction:
Define the mandatory decision path of \(\mathscr A\) directly on the raw legal cycle fiber.  In design A, first test \(m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\); failure is reported as incompatibility.  Otherwise put \(X=\mathcal C_A(T)\).  In design B put \(X=\mathcal C_B(T)\).  Make one bounded-algebraic-sampling call on \(X\).  If \(X\) is empty, report incompatibility.  Otherwise take the returned point \(x_0\), put \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\), and make one existential-realizability call on
\[
X\cap\left\{x:
(\tau_{C,1}(x)-t_{0,1})^2+(\tau_{C,2}(x)-t_{0,2})^2>0
\right\}.
\]
If this refinement is empty, return \(t_0\); otherwise return its sampled point together with \(x_0\) and lift them to legal target-changing full SCMs.  Separately, \(\mathscr A\) may enumerate labeled candidate charts formed from the oriented rank-two, \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) rank-one, support-face, shared-endpoint, and design-B residual-forest modes as structural diagnostics; that enumeration is not consulted by the mandatory rigidity decision.  All symbolic arithmetic is over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), or over the finite real algebraic extension generated by \(t_0\) during the single refinement test.

proposed.statement:
For every fixed finite \((\mathcal W,\mathcal Z)\), the following finite structural atlas is exhaustive.  It rejects a cell whose observed matrix has rank exceeding two.  A rank-two cell is represented by its two oriented segment modes, refined by all coefficient-support faces.  A rank-one cell is represented by the disjoint \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes of the rank-one normal-form lemma, with the \(\mathrm E\) mode split coordinatewise.  Products of the four local modes use one shared variable \(b_i\) at each response vertex, fix proxy supports, and retain endpoint equalities and inequalities, observed-line incidences, and guarded nonzero pivots as polynomial sign atoms.  If \(X^A_\chi\) denotes the resulting design-A charts, then
\[
\bigcup_\chi X^A_\chi=\mathcal C_A(T).
\]
In design B, adjoining \(\rho\), the zero-residual or active negatively proportional state at each response type, lexicographic nonzero pivots, forest propagation, active-cycle product-one constraints, positive component scales, normalization, and a signed relevance witness gives charts satisfying
\[
\bigcup_\chi X^B_\chi=\mathcal C_B(T).
\]
Writing \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), the numbers of labeled templates are at most
\[
M_A=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4,
\qquad
M_B=M_A\,k(k-1)(2k-1)^4.
\]
Every chart has a finite Boolean semialgebraic description over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), including every zero-support and coincident-endpoint face.  Thus the atlas is an exact field-tier structural classification and may be used to label or diagnose a raw-fiber output.  It is not a computational prerequisite for the direct raw-fiber rigidity decision made by \(\mathscr A\).
proposed.justification: This theorem proves that the finite orientation, rank-one, support-face, shared-endpoint, and residual-forest atlas is an exact structural cover of both raw legal cycle fibers.
proposed.gap: The structural atlas is valuable for boundary labels and explanations, but its enumeration is unnecessary for deciding whether the causal target is constant.
proposed.consumer: Analysts and implementations may attach an exact rank, support, and residual-forest diagnosis to a raw-fiber decision without making that atlas part of the minimal decision path.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This replacement removes the raw target decision from the structural theorem, records the retained exact unions and template counts, and updates its proof dependencies.

proposed.statement:
For design A, \(\mathscr A\) first tests \(m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\).  If this test fails, or if the single bounded-algebraic-sampling call on the raw legal fiber \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) reports emptiness, then \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)=\varnothing\); the input is reported as incompatible and is not rigid under \(|\mathcal T_A(p,m)|=1\).  Otherwise let \(x_0\in\mathcal C_A(T)\) be the returned sample and set \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\).  Then \(|\mathcal T_A(p,m)|=1\) if and only if the single raw-fiber refinement
\[
\mathcal C_A(T)\cap\left\{x:
(\tau_{C,1}(x)-t_{0,1})^2+(\tau_{C,2}(x)-t_{0,2})^2>0
\right\}
\]
is empty.  For design B, emptiness of the single sampling call on \(\mathcal C_B(T)\) is equivalent to \(\mathcal F_B(p)=\varnothing\), and, on a nonempty fiber, the analogous single refinement is empty if and only if \(|\mathcal T_B(p)|=1\).

For an arbitrary real input \(\zeta\), a rigid value is returned as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only when the compiler constructs such an expression; every other value is returned as a uniquely ordered real element of a finite algebraic extension, encoded by a square-free real-univariate polynomial over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), rational coordinate functions, and Thom sign data.  For rational \(\zeta\), the encoding may be normalized to a square-free integer polynomial and rational isolating data.  Every nonrigid output contains two legal full SCMs with identical observables and identical supplied margins when margins are supplied, but different \(\tau\).  If both raw-fiber witnesses lie in interior support charts, their full-SCM lifts can be chosen strictly positive; no strict-positivity claim is made for a witness on a boundary face.  The exhaustive structural atlas may label the output diagnostically, but neither its enumeration nor a connected-component description is used in the rigidity decision.
proposed.justification: This theorem is the necessary-and-sufficient causal classifier: after the strict design-A margin check, one raw-fiber sample and one one-copy unequal-target test return incompatibility, the unique target, or legal target-changing SCM twins.
proposed.gap: Regular inversion does not decide target constancy on singular and boundary fibers, but structural chart enumeration is not needed to perform the global constancy test.
proposed.consumer: Analysts receive the minimal exact decision engine, while the separate structural atlas remains available when an explanatory boundary label is wanted.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This replacement states the exact two-call raw-fiber classifier and removes the obsolete dependency on structural chart enumeration while preserving incompatibility, exact-output, legal-twin, and boundary qualifications.

proposed.statement:
Put \(k=|\mathcal Z|\), \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), and
\[
\begin{array}{lll}
N_A=4\ell+8k,&
S_A=4k\ell+4\ell+12k+4,&
D_A=2,\\
N_B=4\ell+9k+8,&
S_B=4k\ell+2k^2+4\ell+15k+15,&
D_B=3.
\end{array}
\]
The raw design-A fiber has a Boolean semialgebraic description with at most \((N_A,S_A,D_A)\) variables, polynomial sign atoms, and polynomial degree, and the raw design-B fiber has one with at most \((N_B,S_B,D_B)\).  The single squared unequal-target atom does not increase either degree bound.  For \(d\in\{A,B\}\), let
\[
(A_{S,d},D_{S,d})=\mathsf{Samp}(N_d,S_d,D_d),
\qquad
(A_{E,d},D_{E,d})=\mathsf{Exist}(N_d,S_d+1,D_d),
\]
where these are coordinatewise nondecreasing published record-count and relative algebraic-degree bounds for bounded algebraic sampling and existential realizability over the current coefficient field.  Define
\[
R_d=2+A_{S,d}+A_{E,d},
\qquad
\mathcal D_d=D_{S,d}D_{E,d},
\qquad
R_{k,\ell}=\max_{d\in\{A,B\}}R_d,
\qquad
\mathcal D_{k,\ell}=\max_{d\in\{A,B\}}\mathcal D_d.
\]
Then \(R_d\) bounds all algebraic sample and decision records generated by the mandatory design-\(d\) raw-fiber path, and \(\mathcal D_d\) bounds the degree over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) of every final real-univariate target or witness coordinate after tower normalization.  These bounds contain no structural-template multiplier and no chart auxiliary variables.  The optional diagnostic atlas nevertheless terminates and has at most
\[
M_A=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4,
\qquad
M_B=M_A\,k(k-1)(2k-1)^4
\]
labeled templates.

If \(Q=k\ell+k^2+\ell+1\), there is a universal constant \(C\geq1\), independent of \(k\), \(\ell\), and the input, such that
\[
R_{k,\ell}\leq2^{CQ^C},
\qquad
\mathcal D_{k,\ell}\leq2^{CQ^C}.
\]
Over an arbitrary real input field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), the computation terminates relative to effective field arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles.

For rational input coordinates whose numerators and denominators have binary length at most \(L\), set
\[
h_0=64Q^2(L+1),
\qquad
h_{S,d}=\mathsf{Samp}_h(N_d,S_d,D_d,h_0),
\]
\[
h_{E,d}=\mathsf{Exist}_h(N_d,S_d+1,D_d;h_0,h_{S,d},D_{S,d}),
\qquad
h_{F,d}=\mathsf{Flat}_h(\mathcal D_d,h_{S,d}+h_{E,d}+1),
\]
and
\[
H_{k,\ell}(L)=
\max_{d\in\{A,B\}}\max\{h_{S,d},h_{E,d},h_{F,d}\}.
\]
After flattening the extension tower and clearing only nonzero observable normalizing denominators, every algebraic target or witness coordinate has a square-free integer polynomial of degree at most \(\mathcal D_{k,\ell}\) and rational isolating data of binary length at most \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\).  After enlarging the same universal constant if necessary,
\[
H_{k,\ell}(L)
\leq
\bigl[64Q^2(L+2)\bigr]^{2^{CQ^C}}.
\]
Thus the mandatory decision consists of one raw-fiber sampling call followed, when nonempty, by one raw-fiber unequal-target existential call.  It does not enumerate charts, describe connected components, project a target image, or use a generic two-copy classifier.  A rational-input Turing implementation terminates.
proposed.justification: This theorem counts the one sampling call and one existential call made by the raw-fiber engine and proves the normalized degree bound by multiplying their sequential extension degrees.
proposed.gap: The prior bound charged the decision for optional chart enumeration and auxiliary residual-forest variables, obscuring the lower degree and record complexity of the raw legal fibers.
proposed.consumer: Exact implementations receive design-specific raw degrees, no template multiplier, singly exponential fixed-alphabet record and degree bounds, and a separately composed rational-height guarantee.

prose_updates.tldr: For every fixed finite four-response-type selected proxy model, PN/PS rigidity is decided directly on the raw legal cycle fiber.  After the strict supplied-margin check in design A, the compiler makes one bounded-algebraic-sampling call and, when the fiber is nonempty, one one-copy unequal-target existential call.  It returns incompatibility, an exact common target, or legal same-observable SCM twins.  A separate exhaustive rank-two, L/R/E/D, support-face, shared-endpoint, and relevant-IV residual-forest atlas supplies optional structural labels but is not queried by the decision engine.  The published regular formulas retain their existing transfer scope; the contribution remains classification of additional compatible singular and boundary laws.  Fixed-alphabet sample-record and algebraic-degree bounds are singly exponential, rational height has a separate conservative bound, and the accepted Wald, exact-coverage, and locally saturated Hausdorff qualifications are unchanged.

The normalized design-A and design-B legal fibers are themselves bounded one-copy semialgebraic sets, so global constancy is decided by comparing every feasible point with one sampled target in a single existential query.  The exhaustive orientation, rank-one, support-face, shared-endpoint, and residual-forest charts remain a separate exact explanation of every singular and boundary configuration.

At the selected-law factorization level, the present finite four-type model specializes their Condition 1.  The fixed-margin two-proxy fiber is a restriction to which Theorem 1 applies, while the relevant-IV fiber satisfies equation (13) and relevance, so Corollary 1 applies directly.  Our contribution does not extend their regular formula or subsume their model; it classifies additional compatible singular and boundary fibers and reports incompatible inputs separately.  Shingaki and Kuroki (2023) and Kawakami (2021) provide separate experimental and IV-plus-proxy overlap results under their own conditions.  Nonnegative-factorization rigidity work supplies geometric context but not causal target constancy on this labeled response cycle.  Basu, Pollack, and Roy (2006) supply the exact bounded-algebraic-sampling, existential-realizability, real-univariate, sign, and root-isolation algorithms used by the two-call raw-fiber engine and, optionally, by structural diagnostics.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The result is a theorem-level exact symbolic procedure, not a claim of a completed production implementation or favorable growing-alphabet complexity.  The mandatory decision works on the raw legal fiber and makes at most one sampling and one unequal-target existential call.  The finite structural atlas can be produced diagnostically but is not required for compatibility or rigidity.  Over arbitrary real observables, computation is relative to effective coefficient-field arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles.  A rational expression is returned only when constructed; otherwise the result remains a real-univariate and Thom encoding.  The singly exponential statement covers fixed-alphabet record count and algebraic degree only; rational coefficient and isolating-endpoint height obey the separate displayed power bound.  Strictly positive twins require both cycle witnesses to lie in interior support charts.  The accepted exact-coverage and locally saturated Hausdorff qualifications are unchanged.  The released numerical GEUVADIS count table and binarization thresholds remain unavailable in the frozen materials, so no numerical dataset verdict is asserted.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The mathematical contribution is an exact fixed-alphabet raw-fiber rigidity decision together with a separate exhaustive response-cycle structural atlas.  Design-A margins outside the strict interior and empty raw fibers are reported as incompatibility, which is non-rigid under the cardinality-one definition.  One raw-fiber sample and one unequal-target existential query decide global constancy across all components and support faces; the chart atlas supplies optional diagnoses rather than a computational prerequisite.  The regular two-proxy result transfers only by restricting Condition 1 to a fixed population margin, and the regular IV result transfers through equation (13) and Corollary 1; the new result adds compatible singular and boundary classification, not a new regular formula or blanket subsumption.  Record/output count and normalized algebraic degree receive singly exponential fixed-alphabet bounds from the two sequential raw-fiber calls and explicit multiplication of extension degrees.  Rational height receives a separate conservative bound.  The statistical Wald, exact-coverage, and locally saturated Hausdorff scopes remain unchanged.  The GEUVADIS application remains an audit protocol conditional on the graph and recovery of the actual released table, not a new numerical reanalysis.
